items.stem: What does set -o pipefail change about a pipeline's exit status?

options.text: The pipeline fails if any command in it fails, not just the last
options.rationale: Without pipefail only the last command's status counts; pipefail surfaces earlier failures.

options.text: It makes every pipeline always succeed
options.rationale: It is the opposite: it propagates failures.
Pipes still work; only status handling changes.

items.explanation: Without pipefail only the last command's status counts; pipefail surfaces earlier failures.

items.stem: Select TWO reasons to quote "${arr[@]}" when iterating a Bash array.

options.text: Each element is preserved as a single word even if it contains spaces
options.rationale: Quoting [@] yields one word per element.

options.text: It prevents elements from being split or glob-expanded
options.rationale: Quoting stops word-splitting and globbing of element contents.

options.text: It converts the array to an associative array
options.rationale: Quoting does not change the array type.

items.explanation: Quoting [@] yields one word per element.

items.stem: Why use trap 'cleanup' EXIT in a script that creates a temporary file?

options.text: It runs cleanup when the script exits for any reason, removing the temp file
options.rationale: An EXIT trap ensures cleanup on normal exit, errors and signals.

options.text: It prevents the script from ever exiting
options.rationale: The trap runs at exit; it does not block exit.
trap does not affect set -e behaviour.

options.text: It automatically compresses the temp file
options.rationale: trap runs a handler; it does not compress.

items.explanation: An EXIT trap ensures cleanup on normal exit, errors and signals.
